Practitioner’s Note: GCash is distribution without protocol visibility: Ethereum matters only if embedded in partner settlement layers; adoption is policy- and partner-driven rather than product-driven.
Practitioner Validation Check: Is geographic focus a hard design constraint, and does Ethereum materially enable settlement somewhere in the payment stack? Yes (indirect / partner-mediated)
Ethereum Dependency Level: Minimal–Replaceable (Ethereum optional and invisible)

Primary Function: Onchain fiat payments and settlement via regulated e-money
Local Problem Addressed: Fragmented European payments, limited programmability of bank money, lack of compliant onchain euros
Ethereum Role in Stack: Native settlement layer (e-money issued directly on Ethereum)
Is Ethereum Abstracted from End Users?: No (onchain balances are first-class monetary objects)
Supported Ethereum Networks: Ethereum Mainnet; Ethereum L2s (e.g., Optimism, Arbitrum)
Local Currency Support: Yes (EUR, GBP, ISK)
FX Model: Onchain settlement with offchain banking rails for redemption; FX external
Key Payment Corridors: Intra-EEA; onchain ↔ SEPA bank accounts
Regulatory Posture: Fully regulated E-Money Institution (EMI)
Custody Model: Non-custodial onchain balances; regulated redemption accounts
Transaction Scale: Low- to high-value (enterprise and treasury flows)
Primary Dependency Risks: Banking partners, regulatory changes to EMI frameworks
Failure Mode: Issuance paused; redemption restricted; fallback to SEPA rails
Description: Monerium issues fully regulated e-money directly on Ethereum, enabling onchain euro, pound, and krona balances that can move natively on public blockchains while remaining redeemable 1:1 into the European banking system.
Reason for Inclusion: Monerium qualifies as a Regional Payment Network because it is structurally constrained to Europe by regulation and uses Ethereum as the primary settlement layer for compliant fiat payments, not merely as a backend optimization.
Practitioner’s Note: Monerium is Europe’s cleanest fiat–Ethereum bridge: unlike stablecoins, money is issued as e-money onchain, making Ethereum part of the regulated monetary perimeter.
Practitioner Validation Check: Is the payment network regionally constrained by regulation, and does Ethereum serve as the authoritative settlement layer for fiat-denominated value? Yes
Ethereum Dependency Level: Critical (Ethereum is the monetary rail, not optional)

Description: MoneyGram is one of the world’s largest remittance networks. Through integrations with stablecoin issuers such as Circle, it has used Ethereum-based USDC settlement to optimize cross-border liquidity and reduce pre-funding requirements, while keeping blockchain fully abstracted from consumers.
Reason for Inclusion: MoneyGram qualifies as a Regional Payment Network because it is structurally anchored in U.S.-origin remittance corridors and uses Ethereum-based stablecoin settlement as backend infrastructure for regional cross-border flows.
Practitioner’s Note: MoneyGram is legacy distribution + modern settlement: Ethereum’s value is operational—liquidity efficiency and faster hub-to-hub settlement—rather than product-level differentiation.
Practitioner Validation Check: Is geographic focus a hard constraint of the remittance network, and does Ethereum materially improve settlement efficiency even if users never see it? Yes
Ethereum Dependency Level: Important (improves liquidity efficiency but replaceable)
